reason: E1 and E3 directly support that Mo and Si additions induce FCC to BCC transformation and increase strength/hardness, but none of the cited evidence addresses the key premise that these phases reinforce the passive film or improve corrosion resistance, which is central to the hypothesis.
premises: Microalloying with Mo or Si induces a partial FCC to BCC phase transformation in HEAs.
This phase transformation increases hardness and mechanical strength.
The phase transformation or secondary phases reinforce the passive film, improving corrosion resistance.
The combined effect simultaneously enhances resistance to wear and corrosion.
There is an optimal microalloying range; excessive additions cause brittleness.
